notes: Circuit taken from the two Fritzing images: LDR leg 1 and the 3V3 lead share column 1; LDR leg 2, capacitor positive leg and the GPIO4 lead share column 3; capacitor negative leg and the GND lead share column 5. Breadboard bank 'b' (rows f-j) used as in the second image.
rpi-4b catalogue entry only lists GPIO_HEADER; I named header pins as ports on the board (3V3 = pin 1, GPIO4 = pin 7, GND.1 = pin 6, GND.2 = pin 9, GPIO17 = pin 11) as the task instructs.

Buzzer: positive leg (port 1) to GPIO17 via column 30, negative leg (port 2) to GND via column 29, per the second image. Wires use male-female leads (male end 'a' on breadboard, female end 'b' on Pi pin); the buzzer uses two extra leads beyond the 3 listed.
Capacitor-1uf and drinking-straw were not in the supplied catalogue text, so I defined them as new part types.
The laser pointer is placed with no electrical edges because it is battery-powered and only aimed down the straw. The LDR sits inside the straw (contact edge).

Not modelled: the 3 socket-socket jumper leads (final enclosure build, an alternative way to connect the LDR and capacitor without the breadboard) and the optional 3.5mm speakers (alternative to the buzzer, plugged into the Pi's audio jack, which is not a port on the catalogue entry).
